### `.changeset/6349-types-internal-name-collisions-batch-2.md`

- names `app.ts` → `packages/types/src/app.ts` — edited by this change

  > **`MenuItem` — renamed to `AppMenuItem` in `app.ts`.** `app.ts` declared a flat, all-optional `interface` (`type?: 'item' | 'group' | 'separator'`, `label`, `icon`, `path`, `href`, `children`, `badge`, `hidden`) — the `@deprecated` legacy navigation item that `AppComponentSchema.menu`, `AppAction.items` and `menuItemToNavigationItem` read. `overlay.ts` declared a discriminated **union**, `MenuCommandItem | MenuDividerItem`, whose command arm requires `label` and whose both arms **tombstone** `type` as `type?: never` (objectui#6523) — precisely the key `app.ts` declares as a three-value enum. Re-pointing either at the other would have made an authored `type: 'separator'` legal on one side and a type error on the other, so the two names had to part. `@object-ui/types` continues to publish overlay's union as `MenuItem` and app's interface as `AppMenuItem`, exactly as before.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Validator relaxation against the spec 17.5.0 accept set — right, and the one divergence is stated correctly.** Read at objectstack `0f6dcac5e9`: `BaseNavItemSchema.label` is `I18nLabelSchema.optional()` and is spread into all eight entry branches (`object`, `dashboard`, `page`, `url`, `report`, `action`, `component`, `doc`, `group`); the separator spreads nothing and carries no label. `I18nLabelSchema` is `z.union([z.string(), InlineLocaleMapSchema])` with no minimum length, so the spec base does accept `''`. The mirror's superRefine now re-imposes `id` only and refuses `label === ''` with the omit-the-key message; the divergence is real, is named in code, changeset and PR body, and sits on the safe side (an empty present label would render empty text and silently opt the entry out of inheritance). The new pin `nav-label-optional-9868` measures the spec per objectui entry type before asserting the mirror, and asserts the parsed entry carries no `label` key — the "parse adds nothing" half the upstream pin required. Pre-existing and unchanged: the mirror admits a plain-string label only (`z.string().optional()`), narrower than the spec's union; not this card.
2. **`NavigationEntryItem.label` optional, and the two raw readers the `tsc` sweep found — right as far as the diff reaches.** `useNavPins` now stores `resolveNavItemLabel(item)`; verified at the head that `UnifiedSidebar` filters `type: 'nav'` favorites out of its Favorites list ("rendered in the Pinned section above by NavigationRenderer"), so that stored label is a placeholder. The mobile tab bar in `AppSchemaRenderer` reads `resolveNavItemLabel(item)` with no `t`, identical to the old `resolveLabel(item.label)` for a present label. But the sweep's instrument sees only reads whose parameter type refuses `undefined`; two guarded runtime readers in the same package escaped it — findings 1 and 2 under ③.
3. **`resolveNavItemLabel` order — right.** At the head: the separator returns `''`; then `item.label === undefined` returns `inheritedNavItemLabel(item, targetLabel)`; only then `resolveLabel(item.label, t)`, whose body reads `label.key` for a non-string and would throw on `undefined`. The ladder: an `object` entry with a `viewName` asks the view, then the object, then falls to `viewName`; an `object` entry asks the object, then `objectName`; a `dashboard` asks the dashboard, then `dashboardName`; every other type shows its target name (`pageName`, `reportName`, `url`, `componentRef`, `actionDef.actionName`); a group or an entry missing its target shows its `id`. Blank answers count as absent. Keyed on absence alone: the `isCustomized` convention path never consults `targetLabel`, so an authored label spelled like the machine name is not swapped (route B stays refused) — pinned with a spy resolver that is never called.
4. **Public surface — right, and public.** `packages/layout/src/index.ts` does `export * from './NavigationRenderer'`, so `NavLabelTarget`, `NavTargetLabelResolver`, the optional `resolveTargetLabel` prop, the sixth parameter of `resolveNavItemLabel` and the defaulted third parameter of `filterNavigationItems` all publish; all additive. `newPageNavigationItem` / `newDashboardNavigationItem` are module exports NOT re-exported by `hooks/index.ts` or the package index, so app-shell's public surface does not grow. `useNavTargetLabel` is internal.
5. **`useNavTargetLabel` — right; the dev's measurement is confirmed.** `useObjectLabel` at the head: `resolve()` walks the app namespaces' translation bundle and otherwise returns the `fallback` it was handed; `objectLabel` falls back to `objectDef.label`, `viewLabel` to its `fallback`, `dashboardLabel` to `label ?? name`. On the nav path that fallback was the entry's own label, so nothing read the target's metadata — the assumption was false, as measured. The hook reads `MetadataProvider`'s getters: `objects` (with the eagerly loaded `view` type merged into `listViews`, keyed object-dot-key; `UnifiedSidebar` already reads `objects` for its capability gate) and `dashboards` (a lazy getter touched only inside the dashboard case — one list for the type, never one per entry). `resolveViewId` accepts the short and the qualified `viewName`.
